weaknesses.critique: The claim is purely about the magnitude of net income growth (>10%), and the evidence clearly shows 16% growth from $88,136M to $101,832M. There is no causal attribution in the claim to critique, and the numbers are directly stated in the 10-K filing comparing FY2025 to FY2024. The fiscal year periods align correctly (June 30, 2025 vs June 30, 2024).

While the evidence shows the net income increase is 16%, I did not examine whether there were any one-time items, extraordinary gains/losses, or accounting changes that might have artificially inflated the FY2025 net income. Evidence E4 mentions 'Net recognized losses on investments' increased and 'Other, net' shows significant losses including losses on equity method investments in OpenAI, which actually worked against net income growth. This suggests the operational performance was even stronger than the 16% headline figure.

The claim makes a straightforward numeric assertion about year-over-year growth exceeding 10%, which is clearly supported by the 16% figure in E5. There are no alternative interpretations of fiscal year periods or ambiguity about what constitutes 'net income' that would weaken this conclusion. The evidence is from the official 10-K filing and directly compares the two fiscal years in question.
